generation.explanation: The sine graph is wavy because sine comes from going around a circle. Picture a point moving around a circle of radius 1. At angle θ, sin θ is just the point's height. As it goes around, it rises to the top (height 1), drops back through the middle (0), sinks to the bottom (−1), and climbs back again. If you plot that height against the angle, you get a smooth wave. The wave repeats every 2π because every full turn brings the point back to where it started. In the animation, turn on "Auto spin" or drag the angle slider. The green height on the circle traces out the blue curve.
